questions.prompt: In which part of a cell does most aerobic respiration take place?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration happens mainly in the **mitochondria**, which is why very active cells such as muscle cells have many of them.

questions.prompt: Select **all** the substances that are produced by aerobic respiration.
questions.explanation: $\text{glucose} + \text{oxygen} \rightarrow \text{carbon dioxide} + \text{water} + \text{energy}$. Oxygen and glucose are used up; lactic acid is made only in anaerobic respiration in muscles.

questions.prompt: Green plants respire only at night, when they are not photosynthesising.
questions.explanation: All living cells respire all the time, day and night. In daylight a plant also photosynthesises, but its cells are still respiring.

questions.prompt: 180 g of glucose releases about 2880 kJ by aerobic respiration and about 150 kJ by anaerobic respiration in muscles. How many times more energy does aerobic respiration release? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: $\frac{2880}{150} = 19.2$, so aerobic respiration releases about 19 times more energy from the same mass of glucose.

questions.prompt: Which substance builds up in human muscles during hard exercise, when they respire without enough oxygen?
questions.explanation: In muscles, anaerobic respiration is $\text{glucose} \rightarrow \text{lactic acid} + \text{a little energy}$. The lactic acid causes tiredness and cramp.

questions.prompt: A farmer in Musanze stores freshly harvested Irish potatoes in a closed pit with no ventilation. After two weeks the potatoes are warm and have lost mass. Explain these observations.
questions.marking_guide: 1 mark: the potato cells are alive and carry out respiration. 1 mark: respiration releases energy, some as heat, so the store warms up (heat cannot escape without ventilation). 1 mark: stored food (starch/glucose) is broken down into carbon dioxide and water, which leave the potatoes, so they lose mass. 1 mark: with no ventilation the oxygen is used up / carbon dioxide builds up, so cells may respire anaerobically and the potatoes start to rot; good ventilation keeps the store cool.
questions.explanation: Living potato cells keep respiring after harvest. Respiration uses up stored food (loss of mass) and releases heat, which builds up in a closed store. Ventilation removes heat and supplies oxygen.
